sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year, from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F203][F1][F10].
Operating income compounded faster at 12.3% [F204], as operating margin rose from 3.2% in FY2017 to 3.9% in FY2026 [F23][F32].
FY2021 and FY2022 are the inflection years, with revenue growth of 17.5% and 15.8% [D189][D238].
In FY2021 the filing attributes the growth to comparable sales up 16% and new warehouses, with e-commerce and gasoline strong in the ancillary businesses [P56][D189].
In FY2022 comparable sales rose 14%, growth was strongest in gasoline, business centers and travel, and inflation was higher than in prior years [P42][D238].
FY2026 net sales rose 10%, mostly from comparable sales up 8%, made up of a 5% rise in average ticket and a 3% rise in shopping frequency, plus 25 net new warehouses [P14][D434].
Warehouse ancillary and other businesses added 3.7pp of revenue growth on 19.9% growth, lifting their share of revenue to 20.2% [D601][D600][D599].
Food and Sundries, the largest category at 38.5% of revenue, added 2.6pp [D558][D560].
The cited passages do not explain why the ancillary businesses accelerated from 2.4% growth in FY2025 [D597].
By segment, the United States contributed 7.2pp of growth and 72.5% of revenue [D672][D670].
Operating income grew 12.5% against revenue growth of 10.1% [D435][D434], an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D457].
Diluted EPS grew 14.0% against net income growth of 13.9%, because the diluted share count fell only 0.1% [D438][D436][D452].
Operating margin of 3.9% in FY2026 is the window high, above the 3.4% median and the 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690].
Against retail peers (n=6) it sits at the 17th percentile, with the peer median at 5.0% [D709][D710].
The FY2026 gain of 0.1pp came from SG&A (+0.1pp) while cost of revenue was neutral [D447][D460][D459].

SG&A as a share of net sales fell 10 basis points, while gross margin percentage fell three basis points as faster growth in lower-margin ancillary businesses such as gasoline and pharmacy shifted the mix [P9][P12][D460].

The largest move in the window was FY2024 at +0.3pp, led by cost of revenue at +0.4pp, which the filing ties to ancillary businesses and the absence of FY2023 charter shipping charges [P24][D349][D361].
Margin gains now come from SG&A leverage and mix, while core merchandise margin is slipping, which makes the 3.9% level [F32] harder to extend.
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income of $9.23 billion [F82][F42][D421].
Free cash flow of $9.38 billion was 1.02x net income, near the 0.99x window median [F102][D422][D701].
Operating cash flow rose because of higher operating income and a smaller net investment in inventories, from faster turns and better supplier payment terms [P6][D439].
Capex of 2.1% of revenue was 2.41x D&A, up from 1.83x in FY2017, and free cash flow margin was 3.1% against a 2.8% median [D417][D423][D11][D418][D698].
Net cash rose to $15.1 billion from $9.50 billion, or 5.0% of revenue [D427][D378][D428].
That is the 100th percentile among six retail peers, whose median is net debt of 4.4% of revenue [D715][D716].
The current ratio was 1.06x against a 1.02x window median [F182][D704].
Current debt rose to $2.25 billion from $75 million, while noncurrent long-term debt fell to $3.91 billion [X160][X159][F192].
Dividends of $2.46 billion and buybacks of $848 million used 35.2% of free cash flow [X120][X110][D430].
Buybacks left the diluted share count 0.1% lower, with $1,115 million of authorization remaining [D452][P3].
Return on average equity was 28.4% against a 24.0% peer median (n=5), at the 60th percentile [D433][D720][D719].
Core merchandise gross margin fell 11 basis points on mix and co-branded card reward costs, while total gross margin percentage fell three basis points [P12].
This matters because the margin gain depends on lower-margin ancillary sales and SG&A leverage [D460].
Receivables grew 23.6% against revenue growth of 10.1%, after 17.7% and 19.1% in the prior two years [D455][D434][D406][D357].
The balance is small at 5 days of sales [D431], but the persistent gap with revenue growth is worth tracking, and the cited passages do not explain it.
Capex grew 17.0% against revenue growth of 10.1%, and capex to D&A rose from 2.27x to 2.41x [D441][D434][D374][D423].
Free cash flow conversion depends on this spending not outrunning operating cash flow growth of 18.6% [D439].
No red-flag candidates were supplied, and no data checks affect these figures.
Operating margin holding at or above 3.9% would confirm the leverage story, while a fall toward the 3.4% median would reverse it [F32][D692], in the FY2027 10-K.
Free cash flow to net income falling below the 0.99x window median would signal that capex or working capital is eroding conversion, against 1.02x now [D422][D701], in the FY2027 10-K.
Capex to D&A rising above 2.41x would mean investment is still accelerating [D423], in the FY2027 10-K.
Worldwide member renewal falling below 89.8% would reverse the membership fee strength of +11% [P13], in the FY2027 10-K.
